intent.quote: Plumb should fix those problems during the design/development instead of afterwards. Understand what happens and why this happens and how to prevent this. SR overlap, SR that should be modified on new intent, SR contradiction,  missing tests,  no earlier version, failing tests should be leveraging plumb mechanisms to prevent this type of issiue.
intent.readback: plumb exists to keep what you mean and what is being built in step. It catches drift while the work happens: in the turn that leaves a link stale, a change unowned or a record silently out of date, and at the merge at the latest, never afterwards. What the recorded intent and the judge can settle is settled without you; you are asked only when your intent itself would change.
will: Tell the agent right after an edit which links it made stale, and keep the turn open until each is resolved.

Repin silently when the covering tests pass and the judge says the meaning is kept; reword a record that drifted from its intent; send a change that breaks intent with no request behind it back to the agent as development work.
Ask you, through the question tool, only when a change would change or drop confirmed intent, or two confirmed records contradict and no recorded intent settles it.
Catch the same for agents a workflow runs, and hold a merge carrying new stale links, links to untested files or untraced changes.
Show, as hints only, records with no link that may depend on a changed record.
Name changed source that no requirement owns, with the judge's proposed owner, in the turn it appears.
wont: Ask you about a refactor or any change the judge finds keeps the meaning.
Write a link, mark a link stale or confirm a record from a hint or a proposal.
Decide a verdict by rule when no judge is reachable: it says so and holds the step.
Leave drift to be found afterwards, or run the full suite routinely to find it.
assumptions: Drift means code, tests or records no longer matching the confirmed intent: stale links, links to untested files, pins to uncommitted versions, changes no requirement owns, and unlinked records that may depend on a change.
'The judge' is P8's: JEV above its calibrated threshold, else the configured judge model; a repin or rewording it validates counts as approved (P3, P9).
A case plumb cannot settle (a plumb bug, missing information) goes to the debug workflow, not to the owner (P5).
The scan limits (5 candidates, 1 second) are defaults the owner may raise in plain words (P13).
Only records are the specification (P15), so a changed document no longer triggers the dependency scan.

requirements.title: Drift on linked code is resolved in the turn that makes it
requirements.statement: After each edit plumb tells the agent which links it made stale, and the end-of-turn hook holds the turn while a link this turn made stale is unresolved, at most hooks.stale_holds_max times (3 by default); after that the turn ends and the unresolved link becomes one question through the question tool. A check that waits on an unreachable judge never holds the turn. The link is repinned when covering tests pass and the judge says the meaning is kept, a record that disagrees with its intent is reworded, an unrequested intent-breaking change goes back to the agent, and the owner is asked through the question tool only when confirmed intent would change. Workflow agents get the same.

examples.then: the agent is told SR-032 may no longer agree with that intent

examples.then: the judge (JEV above its calibrated threshold, else the configured judge model) is shown SR-003's statement and examples next to the diff, says the meaning is kept, and the link is repinned and logged with its one-sentence reason; the owner is not asked

proof.plan: Recommended for the owner to decide: in a live session on a scratch repository with one confirmed requirement, the agent refactors its code (the plumb line shows the link repinned with the judge's reason, no question), then deletes the test of one confirmed example (the turn stays open naming the link for at most three holds, and one question reaches the owner through the question tool).

requirements.title: Records that may silently depend on a changed record are shown as hints
requirements.statement: When a confirmed record changes, a bounded scan proposes records with no link to it that may depend on what changed, each confirmed by the judge, and shows them to the agent as drift hints; a hint never marks a link stale, adds an edge or interrupts the owner. The scan's limits default to 5 candidates and 1 second, and the owner may raise them. A link to a whole test file gets the test node that checks an example proposed the same way, as a hint.

examples.given: confirmed SR-004 changes and SR-012 shares its key terms with no link
examples.then: a hint says SR-012 may depend on the change to SR-004 and no link state changes

examples.given: 50 candidate records overlap the change and the limits are the defaults
examples.then: at most 5 are judged and the scan ends within 1 second

examples.given: the owner has asked in plain words for a wider scan, and the candidate limit is now 10
examples.when: the scan runs on a change with 50 overlapping candidates
examples.then: at most 10 are judged

examples.given: no judge can be reached
examples.then: plumb says judging is unavailable and shows no hint decided by rule

examples.given: a document under docs/ changes and no record changes

examples.given: SR-001 is verified_by tests/test_calc.py, a test file with test_add_returns_sum inside and no test node named
examples.then: a hint proposes tests/test_calc.py::test_add_returns_sum for SR-001's first example and no link changes

proof.plan: Recommended for the owner to decide: the agent changes one confirmed record in a scratch repository where an unlinked record shares its terms; the agent's reply reports the hint it received naming that record, and the plumb line shows no stale link and no question.

requirements.title: A change no requirement owns gets a judge-proposed owner and is held at merge
requirements.statement: A changed source path no requirement links is untraced: plumb tells the agent in that turn, without blocking, naming the owning requirement the judge proposes among code-map candidates, and plumb review's drift section names the same proposal, uncommitted changes included; the merge is held until a requirement owns it or it is exempted. plumb never writes the link itself. One definition of source code, shared with covering-test selection, decides what is source, flat layouts included. The agent's standing instructions (plumb's CLAUDE.md block) tell it to formalize each request that changes the system into proposed records linked to the code it changes.

examples.given: src/app/mul.py changed with no owner, SR-001 owns src/app/calc.py in the same package, and the judge picks SR-001 among the candidates
examples.then: it names SR-001 as the proposed owner and no link is added

examples.given: no judge can be reached, src/app/mul.py changed with no owner and SR-001 owns src/app/calc.py

examples.given: a turn writes src/app/mul.py and no requirement links it

examples.then: the agent is told both are untraced, without blocking

examples.given: the end-of-turn hook already keeps the turn open to run covering tests
examples.then: the hold's reason also carries the untraced instruction, once

examples.given: SR-001 owns src/app/calc.py, src/app/mod.py is written and not committed, and the judge picks SR-001
examples.then: its drift section names SR-001 as the proposed owner of src/app/mod.py, reading uncommitted changes as the merge check does

proof.plan: Recommended for the owner to decide: in a live session on a flat-layout scratch repository, the agent writes a module no requirement owns; the agent's reply names the module as untraced with the judge's proposed owner, and no link is written; the merge check then holds the branch naming the path until the agent links it.

requirements.title: A commit is warned, never held, when the judge says its diff does not serve the requirement it claims
requirements.statement: At commit, the judge reads the diff against each requirement the commit's trailer claims; when it says the diff does not serve one, plumb prints a one-line warning and the commit goes through, the trailer check's result unchanged. With no judge it says judging is unavailable and warns nothing by rule.

examples.given: a commit claiming the requirement for reports that only changes src/app/report.py
examples.when: the commit-msg hook runs and the judge answers that the diff does not serve that requirement
examples.then: it prints one warning line naming the requirement and the commit goes through; the trailer check's result is unchanged

examples.given: no judge can be reached
examples.when: the diff-serves check runs for the same commit
examples.then: it prints one line that judging is unavailable, no warning decided by rule, and the commit goes through

proof.plan: Recommended for the owner to decide: in a scratch repository, the agent commits a change to the report module claiming an unrelated requirement; the commit goes through and its output carries one warning line naming that requirement.

decisions.question: When code or tests linked to a confirmed requirement change, when is the owner asked?
decisions.chosen: Never by default: plumb checks the requirement is still covered (its tests pass and the judge says the meaning is kept) and repins; a change that breaks intent with no request behind it goes back to the agent; the owner is asked, through the question tool, only when confirmed intent would change or two confirmed records contradict with no recorded intent settling it; what cannot settle goes to the debug workflow.
alternatives: A question on every change to what the owner confirmed
A question only on contradictions, everything else settled by the agent

retired_decisions.why: In no cluster but listed under P1: a one-time clean-up of links left stale from before the drift gate; the v2 record set is pinned fresh when it lands, so no pre-gate stale link remains to rule on.
